title.narrative: Improved access to quality jobs in Indonesia's rural economy

description.narrative:
The rural economy plays a vital role in Indonesia’s employment landscape, with over 40% of the population living in villages and depending on agriculture, fisheries, plantations, and micro and small enterprises. These sectors are major job providers and hold strong potential for inclusive and sustainable employment.
However, structural challenges remain, including the dominance of the informal sector, low job quality, and limited access to training, finance, and markets. Social inclusion for women, youth, and vulnerable groups is also limited, requiring integrated solutions through skills development, infrastructure investment, and local economic empowerment.
To address these issues, ILO Indonesia implemented the Promise 2 Impact (P2I) and Coffee Project in 2024–2025 across the coffee, patchouli, seaweed, and dairy cattle sectors. In Lampung, ILO conducted a harvest survey and delivered training on labour rights, OSH, and social protection. In Aceh and West Java, Enterprise Resources Platform (ERP) systems were introduced to strengthen cooperatives and financial access.
In East Nusa Tenggara, ILO promoted inclusive coastal economies through digital tools and social dialogue. In the palm oil sector, ILO and Palm Oil Trade Union Network Indonesia (JAPBUSI) worked together to establish a grievance mechanism for rural workers. In total, 1,029 farmers benefited directly, with thousands more union members expected to benefit.
